edges.description: Loss of the transporter reduces citrate import into neurons.
Failure of cellular NaCT-mediated citrate uptake causes citrate to accumulate in plasma, cerebrospinal fluid, and brain extracellular space.
NaCT is also required in tooth-forming ameloblasts for enamel matrix mineralization.
Loss of NaCT citrate transport during odontogenesis leads to congenitally missing teeth (hypodontia) through incompletely defined developmental intermediates.
Intracellular citrate deficiency disrupts downstream metabolism.
Metabolic and neurotransmitter-precursor disruption dysregulates excitability.
Disrupted neuronal metabolism impairs brain development.
Excess extracellular citrate binds divalent Zn2+ at the neuronal plasma membrane.
Depletion of free extracellular Zn2+ relieves tonic zinc inhibition of NMDA glutamate receptors.
Disinhibited NMDA receptor signaling and unremitting Ca2+ influx drive synchronous neuronal hyperexcitability.
Dysregulated neuronal excitability manifests clinically as tonic and clonic seizures beginning in the first days of life.
Sustained uninhibited hyperexcitability frequently progresses to prolonged seizures and status epilepticus.
Refractory seizure activity and network dysfunction establish a neonatal developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
Impaired brain maturation produces early-onset global developmental delay across motor and cognitive domains.
Persistent neurodevelopmental impairment evolves into severe cognitive impairment and intellectual disability in later childhood.
Central neurodevelopmental dysfunction causes diffuse infantile muscular hypotonia and abnormal tone.
Disrupted motor circuit development leads to extrapyramidal movement disorders including dystonia.
Impaired cerebellar and motor pathway maturation results in impaired coordination and ataxia.
Impaired cortical and motor speech development causes severe expressive and receptive communication impairment.
Impaired central motor maturation markedly delays attainment of gross motor milestones such as sitting and walking.
A minority of affected children experience isolated episodes of motor or language skill loss against a background of persistent developmental delay.
Central neurodevelopmental and network dysfunction disrupts sleep-wake regulation and sleep architecture.
Severe neurologic and oral-motor impairment, compounded by dental abnormalities, contributes to pediatric feeding difficulties.
Defective ameloblast enamel matrix formation and mineralization manifest as tooth enamel hypoplasia and amelogenesis imperfecta.
Elevated plasma and cerebrospinal-fluid citrate reflect failure of NaCT-mediated citrate uptake.

nodes.description: Because antiseizure medications are only partially effective, gene-replacement therapy that restores NaCT is being developed. In a preclinical mouse model, cerebrospinal-fluid AAV9-mediated delivery of functional human SLC13A5 lowered extracellular citrate and rescued epileptic and electrophysiologic phenotypes, and a Phase 1/2 open-label lumbar intrathecal clinical trial of TSHA-105 is registered (NCT07102524).

evidence.reference_title: AAV-mediated gene therapy in a model of SLC13A5 citrate transporter disorder rescues epileptic and metabolic phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: Cerebrospinal fluid delivery of AAV9/SLC13A5 decreased extracellular citrate levels, normalized electrophysiologic and sleep architecture abnormalities, and restored resistance to chemically induced seizures and death.

nodes.description: NaCT is expressed in tooth-forming ameloblasts, where citrate contributes to enamel mineralization. Loss of NaCT impairs enamel matrix formation and maturation, producing the characteristic dental enamel defects (amelogenesis imperfecta).

evidence.reference_title: Defective enamel and bone development in sodium-dependent citrate transporter (NaCT) Slc13a5 deficient mice.
evidence.snippet: Slc13a5 deficiency led to defective tooth development,  characterized by absence of mature enamel, formation of aberrant enamel matrix,  and dysplasia and hyperplasia of the enamel organ epithelium that progressed  with age.
